nodes.label: Trusted Wake Signal
nodes.rationale: The proposal emphasizes wake times because Lunifer knows them more reliably than inferred sleep onset and duration.

nodes.label: Minimal Manual Input
nodes.rationale: The experience should be seamless, keep onboarding short, and avoid asking users to provide data manually.

nodes.label: First-Night Sleep Data Onboarding
nodes.rationale: The empty state sets the expectation that sleep history will populate only after the user's first night, while still showing the configured eight-hour recommendation and available history ranges.

nodes.label: Trusted-Device Sleep Personalization
nodes.rationale: The screen invites users to connect familiar wearable devices so Lunifer can tailor sleep recommendations to their body and visually compare the providers' current sleep-duration signals.

nodes.label: Trusted-Device Sleep Personalization
nodes.rationale: The polished promotional screen presents WHOOP and Oura as trusted inputs for body-tailored sleep recommendations, pairing a visual duration comparison with direct connection actions.

nodes.label: Reliability Evidence Policy
nodes.rationale: A reliability case remains open until a focused reproduction verifies the exact failure mode and recovery behavior.

nodes.label: Actual System Alarm Evidence
nodes.rationale: Scheduling confirmation, notification delivery, and successful wake-up are separate outcomes requiring distinct evidence.

nodes.label: Alarm Permission Recovery Flow
nodes.rationale: When alarm access is disabled, the screen explains that Lunifer cannot set alarms and provides a single action that directs the user to Settings to restore Alarms & Reminders access.

nodes.label: Devices You Trust Message
nodes.rationale: The screen frames WHOOP and Oura as trusted devices whose data personalizes sleep recommendations.

nodes.label: Destructive Continue Emphasis
nodes.rationale: Red marks continuing without calendar access as the riskier path while keeping No in familiar iOS blue.
